title: Automated 2D and 3D Electron Microscopy for Assessing Nanoparticle Degradation on Porous Carbon Supports at the Nanoscale
content: Enhancing the durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) for heavy-duty vehicles (HDVs) is essential for their widespread adoption. The U.S. Department of Energy’s Million Mile Fuel Cell Truck (M2FCT) consortium aims to address this challenge by investigating catalyst degradation mechanisms through advanced characterization techniques. A key objective is to assess the structural and morphological changes in platinum (Pt) nanoparticles and porous carbon supports following accelerated stress testing (AST) protocols for HDV applications [1].
